notes: All measurement phases ran serially. No library implementation changed during the rerun.
Browser timing, browser heap, Node parser heap and Node formatter heap are separate workloads/counters. No total-RAM claim is derived.
Earlier same-library long-fence timings are in 2026-10-23-fences.json and were not rerun in this phase. Active formatter heap is newly measured.
Controlled baseline assets are the final guarded October 22 HTML-addition build. Current harness source and CSS match; frozen assets were copied, not rebuilt or overwritten.
Node fence heap consumes changed code HTML when provided, otherwise complete pending HTML. It excludes DOM operations and does not simulate gutter text insertion.

notes: HTML strings only: excludes formatting hooks, highlighting, DOM, layout, and React.
32 * scale characters per update; this keeps 267 deliveries at all three scales.
Five timed replays after one untimed replay; full/incremental order alternates.
All sampled incremental prefixes are checked against a fresh HTML render outside timing.
Memory is a separate replay after replacing the shared arena. Source is included in baseline.
Heap and Wasm committed bytes are separate counters, not total process memory.
Releasing a session does not shrink the shared Wasm arena; arena bytes are a high-water mark.
Parser APIs only: excludes React, highlighting, token fades, DOM, and browser layout/paint.
Render timings are three samples after a one-unit warmup; append and parity replays run once.
GC and assertions run outside timers. Timed operations may still incur automatic GC.
Inputs are sparse prefixes, not a simulated real-time token stream; do not compare these ratios with 64-character replay benchmarks.
Memory includes the source, module, and harness. heapUsed is JS heap; external and RSS overlap other allocations and are not live-memory sums.
wasmCommittedBytes measures the shared linear-memory high-water mark, not occupied parser data. Replacing the arena is benchmark isolation, not a public trimming API.
A retained session owns completed HTML and the current result strings even after the caller releases its result. Released-output samples keep the current Wasm arena alive.
Parity timing uses a shared arena and alternating order; append-session memory was measured separately before those full parses.

Configured code closure includes TypeScript, default light/dark themes, and highlighted-body lazy chunks.
Pierre includes its monolithic grammar set; Streamdown lazily imports individual grammars.
CSS is separate; application-specific Streamdown Tailwind utility CSS is excluded.
One growing TypeScript fence, about 250 deliveries, alternating complete and partial final lines; final delivery closes the fence.
Node formatter timing requests complete pending HTML and reads its length, even when the DOM can use a suffix. The JavaScript engine may defer copying concatenated strings.

Node runs include one discarded replay and a different-code grammar warmup. Exact code text and gutter parity plus normalized visible-text styling and HTML structure are checked after each timed replay; harmless span coalescing, trailing CSS semicolons, and line-break color differences are normalized.
Browser update time covers flushSync React commit and native DOM patch; later layout and paint are represented by frame intervals and long tasks.
Delay 0 uses separate MessageChannel tasks; positive delay is commit-paced setTimeout, not fixed-rate delivery.
Diagnostic runs alone wrap template.innerHTML and collect mutations; their timings are excluded from primary samples.
No viewport containment, virtualization, scrolling, or animation. Full code height remains in normal document layout.
Separate initial bundles can be retained and rerun with --skip-build. Hashes identify the actual frozen code.
Independent formatter sessions in one warmed Node process; samples are not fresh-process trials.

The full source is materialized as a new flat UTF-8 round-trip string before any baseline, avoiding later rope-flattening allocation in session deltas. No source-prefix arrays or previous result objects are retained by the harness.
One complete replay through live edits, fence closure, empty-source reset, and disposal is discarded before sampling, warming the same session path and shared grammar.
Active means every delivery before the closing fence; code HTML suffixes are consumed when available, otherwise full pending HTML, matching the applicable DOM delivery contract.
Each heap sample follows two explicit garbage collections separated by event-loop turns. Collection is outside performance timing.
Only process.memoryUsage().heapUsed is reported. Native DOM, Wasm commitment, external allocations, graphics, and total process memory are excluded.
Closure, empty-source reset, and disposal plus renderer release are separate stages. Remaining caches or reset deltas do not establish a leak.
